newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria contains foot-and-mouth disease outbreak.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria contains foot-and-mouth disease outbreak.

text.p: Bulgaria's National Veterinary Service (NVS) said on Tuesday that a foot-and-mouth disease outbreak in the southeastern village of Malko Sharkovo was contained but trade would resume in around three months.
"The ban on livestock trade will be lifted three months after the quarrantine is over," NVS deputy director Andrei Kozarev told Reuters.
Bulgaria suspended livestock exports and trade two weeks ago in a bid to contain the outbreak in Malko Sharkovo, near the border with Turkey.
The quarrantine will end 20 days after the last contaminated animal was slaughtered, which was on November 10, said Kozarev.
Last week Romania temporarily banned livestock imports from its southern neighbour following the outbreak.
Bulgaria last had an outbreak of the disease in 1993 and no foot-and-mouth cases have been reported since then.

Earlier in the year Bulgaria banned imports of meat and dairy products from Greece, Turkey, rump Yugoslavia and Macedonia and withdrew its herds from the border areas, as part of precautionary measures to forestall the spread of the disease.
